You are a NEUTRAL AI case assessor supporting an ombudsman in a dispute between Corbel Mutual Insurance (which declined a claim) and Penrose Bakeries Pty Ltd (the insured business).

Question: How likely is it that Corbel Mutual was entitled to decline Penrose Bakeries' claim for non-disclosure? P=0 clearly not entitled; P=50 genuinely balanced; P=100 clearly entitled.

Calibration: P=50 means the evidence so far is genuinely balanced. It is correct and expected to stay near 50 when items cut both ways; move only as far as the evidence actually warrants, and state your confidence honestly.

You will receive the items one at a time. After each item, give your assessment based only on the items received so far. You will not be able to revise earlier assessments.

After each item reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"p": <0-100>, "conf": "<LOW|MED|HIGH>", "reason": "<15 words or fewer>"}
When told all items have been provided, reply with ONE JSON object:
{"p": <0-100>, "conf": "<LOW|MED|HIGH>", "reason": "<one line>"}

exchanges.user:
=== EVIDENCE BUNDLE (submitted by the parties; weigh each item critically, and note that any cover-notes are the parties' own characterisations, not findings) ===
[Instructing note]: Instructing note: Please assess the enclosed bundle in the Corbel/Penrose complaint and give a running, calibrated view on whether the insurer was entitled to decline the claim. The record is mixed; weigh each item on its merits.

=== ITEM 1 ===
The proposal form asked: 'Have you made any insurance claims in the last five years?' The policy lets Corbel refuse a claim if a non-disclosure would have led it to decline cover or to offer cover on materially different terms. Note: refusal is only allowed if the answer would actually have changed the underwriting decision.

Your assessment after item 1:
exchanges.text: {"p": 50, "conf": "LOW", "reason": "Only framework given; no facts yet on answer, claims history, or materiality."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 2 ===
Penrose made a flood claim of AUD 85,000 in 2022, under a different insurer, for the same premises. The proposal form answered the prior-claims question 'No'. Note: the 2022 claim was with another insurer and under a different policy year.

Your assessment after item 2:
exchanges.text: {"p": 68, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Clear wrong answer; question covered any insurer. Underwriting impact still unproven."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 3 ===
The proposal was completed by Penrose's broker. The broker's file note of the call with the owner reads: 'mentioned the 2022 water damage, all repaired'. The broker did not record it on the form. Note: the owner did disclose the earlier claim; the omission was the broker's.

Your assessment after item 3:
exchanges.text: {"p": 62, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Broker usually insured's agent; disclosure to broker isn't to insurer, but negates dishonesty."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 4 ===
Corbel's 2023 underwriting guidelines say a prior flood claim at the same premises requires referral to a senior underwriter and either a flood exclusion or a premium loading of at least 30%. Note: the guideline points to a flood exclusion or loading, not to refusing cover altogether.

Your assessment after item 4:
exchanges.text: {"p": 72, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Exclusion or 30% loading is 'materially different terms', satisfying the policy test."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 5 ===
The current loss is a fire caused by an electrical fault in an oven, assessed at AUD 410,000 including business interruption. The loss adjuster records no connection to any water or flood damage. Note: the fire has nothing to do with the undisclosed flood; a flood exclusion would not have touched this loss.

Your assessment after item 5:
exchanges.text: {"p": 30, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Fire unrelated; likely terms (exclusion/loading) would still cover it, so full refusal doubtful."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 6 ===
Corbel's underwriting file shows that a commercial claims-database check returned 'prior property claim - details unknown' for the address. There is no record that the underwriter followed it up. Note: the insurer was put on notice of a prior claim and chose not to ask.

Your assessment after item 6:
exchanges.text: {"p": 22, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Insurer had notice of prior claim and didn't inquire; waiver/knowledge argument strengthens."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 7 ===
The owner signed the proposal declaration: 'I have read the answers in this proposal and they are true and complete.' Note: a standard declaration signed on a broker-prepared form says little about what the owner actually knew was on it.

Your assessment after item 7:
exchanges.text: {"p": 25, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Declaration confirms responsibility for answer but doesn't fix lack of underwriting prejudice."}

exchanges.user:
=== ITEM 8 ===
Corbel's decline letter cites non-disclosure of the 2022 claim. Penrose's complaint says disclosure was made through its broker and offers to pay any additional premium that would have applied. Note: the insured offered to put the insurer in the position it would have been in had the claim been on the form.

Your assessment after item 8:
exchanges.text: {"p": 20, "conf": "MED", "reason": "Offer to pay extra premium mirrors proportionate remedy; outright decline looks excessive."}

exchanges.user: All items have been provided. Give your FINAL assessment.
exchanges.text: {"p": 20, "conf": "MED", "reason": "The 'No' answer was wrong and the broker's omission binds Penrose. But the likely revised terms (flood exclusion or loading) would still cover this unrelated fire. Corbel also ignored a prior-claim flag, so full refusal looks unjustified."}
